Convergence of Climate Stress and Cyber Warfare

Climate change is placing unprecedented physical stress on global energy grids, municipal water distribution networks, and agricultural infrastructure. Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) groups strategically exploit these vulnerabilities during periods of extreme environmental stress.

Targeting Strained Critical Infrastructure

Nation-state actors recognize that physical infrastructure operating near capacity—such as power grids during severe heatwaves or water management systems during droughts—is exceptionally fragile and vulnerable to cascading disruptions from targeted cyberattacks.

Geopolitical Motivations and APT Tradecraft

Cybelle Oliveira examines the geopolitical motivations driving state-sponsored cyber operations against environmental critical infrastructure, analyzing TTPs used to penetrate OT networks and manipulate supervisory control data.

Defensive Resilience and Strategic Planning

Strengthening infrastructure resilience requires integrating physical climate risk models with cybersecurity threat intelligence, prioritizing fail-safe operations, and hardening critical control loops.

talks.title: Moonlight Defender: Purple Teaming in Space!
talks.teaser: Demonstrates purple team methodologies applied to satellite ground segments and flight software to validate threat detections and improve space cyber defenses.
talks.summary:
Applying Purple Teaming to Space Operations

As space infrastructure becomes increasingly critical for global navigation, communications, and defense, securing satellite architectures requires collaborative, iterative security testing between offensive operators and mission defenders.

Space Attack Surface and Emulation Scenarios

Ben Hawkins details purple teaming exercises targeting satellite ground segment networks, mission command servers, and simulated onboard flight software payloads, emulating realistic adversary techniques.

Validating Telemetry and Anomaly Detections

Executing controlled offensive maneuvers allows space defenders to evaluate whether satellite telemetry pipelines, ground station logs, and ground control monitoring systems correctly identify anomalous command sequences in real time.

Lessons Learned and Operational Hardening

Purple team exercises in space systems reveal critical visibility gaps, enabling mission teams to refine intrusion detection rules, implement cryptographic command verification, and harden ground-to-space communications.

talks.title: Fear vs Physics: Diagnosing Grid Chaos
talks.teaser: Separates cyberattacks from physical power dynamics, analyzing grid oscillations, transformer fires, and blackstart scenarios to diagnose grid disturbances.
talks.summary:
Misconceptions Surrounding Electric Grid Failures

When major power grid disruptions occur, media and analysts frequently rush to suspect malicious cyberattacks. However, the majority of grid disturbances originate from physical power dynamics, equipment physics, and control system interactions.

Low-Frequency Oscillations in Bulk Power Systems

As renewable generation and inverter-based resources expand, low-frequency oscillations increasingly emerge across transmission networks. These oscillations stem from control system tuning and physical network conditions rather than adversarial cyber intrusions.

Analyzing Historical Incidents: Blackouts and Equipment Fires

Emma Stewart dissects real-world power events, including the Iberian Peninsula blackout and the London transformer fire, demonstrating how protection relays acted correctly to preserve equipment and how operational blackstart plans functioned under stress.

Replacing Fear with Engineering Facts

Accurately securing power infrastructure requires deep domain knowledge of power system physics, robust telemetry analysis, and distinguishing physical operational phenomena from genuine cyber threats.

talks.title: What is Dead May Never Die: The Immortality of SDK Bugs
talks.teaser: Explores how unpatched software development kits from major chipset vendors perpetuate persistent vulnerabilities across millions of consumer IoT devices.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquity of Vendor Chipset SDKs

Chipset manufacturers provide Software Development Kits (SDKs) containing reference drivers, pre-compiled binaries, and web management services to help device vendors quickly bring smart hardware to market.

Flaws Frozen in Upstream Codebases

When vulnerabilities exist within reference SDK code, those flaws are bundled into dozens of commercial product lines across multiple vendors. Once hardware is deployed in the field, upstream SDK patches rarely propagate down to end-user devices.

Botnet Exploitation of Zombie SDK Vulnerabilities

Richard Lawshae demonstrates old-day and zero-day vulnerabilities in major chipset SDKs that have been continuously exploited by IoT botnet operators across millions of connected cameras, routers, and smart plugs.

Cleaning the Zombie SDK Ecosystem

Mitigating systemic SDK vulnerabilities requires chipset vendors to adopt transparent patch management, device manufacturers to maintain active firmware update pipelines, and automated SBOM tracking across embedded software.

talks.title: Navigating the Invisible
talks.teaser: Demonstrates low-cost OSINT techniques leveraging vessel tracking, port data, and open intelligence to detect anomalous behavior and maritime security risks.
talks.summary:
Open-Source Intelligence in the Maritime Domain

The vastness of the maritime domain conceals significant operational and cybersecurity risks. Leveraging publicly accessible open-source intelligence (OSINT) allows defenders to build comprehensive threat intelligence pictures without expensive proprietary tooling.

Analyzing Vessel Tracking and AIS Data

Monitoring Automatic Identification System (AIS) broadcasts, vessel registry databases, and port departure logs enables analysts to detect anomalous vessel movements, spoofed location reports, and suspicious offshore rendezvous.

Integrating Port Logistics and Social Media Telemetry

Correlating maritime shipping manifests, satellite imagery, and port worker social media data surfaces hidden supply chain bottlenecks, physical security vulnerabilities, and potential smuggling operations.

Actionable Intelligence for Sector Defenders

Practitioners can implement low-cost data collection workflows and automated alert pipelines to maintain proactive situational awareness across critical maritime shipping lanes.

talks.title: Hull Integrity: Applying MOSAICS to Naval Mission Systems
talks.teaser: Breaks down how the US Department of Defense MOSAICS Block 1 framework provides real-time OT monitoring and behavioral threat detection on Naval vessels.
talks.summary:
Cyber-Physical Attack Surfaces in Naval Fleets

Modern naval vessels integrate interconnected operational technology (OT) systems managing propulsion, electrical power distribution, damage control, and weapons systems, creating complex cyber-physical attack surfaces.

The MOSAICS Block 1 Framework

Developed by the Department of Defense, the More Situational Awareness for Industrial Control Systems (MOSAICS) Block 1 framework establishes reference architectures for real-time asset discovery, monitoring, and behavioral threat detection tailored for mission-critical ICS.

Adapting Reference Architectures to Shipboard Systems

Michael Frank explains how the Department of the Navy adapts MOSAICS to legacy and modern naval systems, overcoming severe constraints regarding compute availability, network bandwidth, and disconnected maritime operations.

Operationalizing OT Defense at Scale

Deploying automated behavioral detection and safe asset inventory aboard naval vessels enhances fleet cyber survivability without interfering with critical mission operations or weapons control.

talks.title: HoloConnect AI: From Space to Biohacking
talks.teaser: Introduces HoloConnect AI, an air-gapped holographic agent running local offline AI models developed for space missions and surgical assistance.
talks.summary:
Air-Gapped Holographic Intelligence

Originally developed and tested aboard the International Space Station (ISS), HoloConnect AI combines holographic display hardware with local, offline artificial intelligence models for environments where cloud connectivity is impossible.

Expanding from Aerospace to Medical Devices

Deploying offline holographic AI agents in healthcare settings enables surgeons and clinicians to interact with voice- and vision-aware AI assistants during complex surgical procedures without risking clinical data exposure.

Secure Embedded Stacks and Voice Spoofing Defense

Operating AI agents on air-gapped embedded hardware requires sandboxed model execution, secure local sensor processing, and acoustic anti-spoofing controls to prevent unauthorized voice actuation.

Live Demonstrations and Future Horizons

Demonstrating medical-grade holographic agents running without external network connectivity highlights how edge AI can deliver instant, private decision support in high-stakes environments.

talks.title: How AI + Hardware can Transforming Point-of-Care Workflows
talks.teaser: Demonstrates custom CM5 and RP2040 embedded hardware paired with local speech and language models for automated offline clinical data logging.
talks.summary:
Bedside Clinical Computing Challenges

Clinical environments produce continuous streams of patient telemetry, diagnostic imaging, and physician notes. However, strict healthcare privacy rules and network instability complicate cloud-based AI assistance at the bedside.

Hardware Architecture: CM5, RP2040, and E-Ink

PamirAI engineers created a dedicated bedside device combining a Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5, an RP2040 microcontroller, and an ultra-low-power E-ink display to run local inference within a tight 10-watt power envelope.

Software Layer and MCP Hub Integration

The embedded software stack features an MCP Hub that translates natural language clinician requests into automated sensor logging and structured record updates without requiring external network connectivity.

Rapid Sensor Integration via Local AI

Leveraging on-device AI models enables rapid integration and calibration of medical telemetry sensors, empowering clinicians with immediate, automated documentation right at the point of care.

talks.title: Firmware Decryption: For, and By, the Cryptographically Illiterate
talks.teaser: Breaks down practical software and hardware techniques for decrypting obfuscated and encrypted IoT firmware without requiring advanced cryptography math.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Encrypted IoT Firmware

Device manufacturers increasingly encrypt and obfuscate firmware update images to thwart reverse engineering and security audits. However, the cryptographic implementations in embedded devices often contain fundamental flaws.

Locating Keys in Hardware and Bootloaders

Craig Heffner demonstrates how security researchers can extract decryption keys from physical flash chips, unencrypted bootloader stages (such as U-Boot), and hardware debug interfaces (JTAG/UART) without advanced mathematical cryptanalysis.

Analyzing Flawed Symmetric Key Implementations

Many vendors rely on static, shared AES keys hardcoded across entire product families or employ flawed XOR and substitution ciphers. Reverse engineering previous unencrypted firmware revisions frequently reveals the decryption routines.

Practical Tooling and Unpacking Workflows

Equipped with practical scripts and firmware analysis frameworks, researchers can successfully unpack encrypted vendor updates and inspect embedded binaries for vulnerabilities.

talks.title: Safeguarding the Industrial Frontier: OT SOC & Incident Response
talks.teaser: Explores specialized incident response strategies and operational considerations required to build and run effective Security Operations Centers in OT environments.
talks.summary:
Bridging IT and OT Security Operations

As industrial enterprises connect operational technology (OT) to enterprise IT networks, building dedicated OT Security Operations Center (SOC) capabilities has become essential to safeguard physical processes from cyber threats.

Unique Operational Constraints in Industrial SOCs

Unlike traditional IT SOCs that focus on data confidentiality and endpoint isolation, OT SOCs prioritize system availability, process safety, and physical uptime. Standard IT containment actions—such as shutting down hosts or blocking subnets—can cause catastrophic physical shutdowns.

Specialized OT Incident Response Playbooks

Adam Robbie details how organizations must develop incident response playbooks tailored to programmable logic controllers (PLCs), distributed control systems (DCS), and proprietary industrial protocols.

Continuous Monitoring and Threat Telemetry

Effective OT defense relies on passive network monitoring, protocol anomaly detection, and close collaboration between cybersecurity analysts and frontline plant control engineers.

talks.title: Your Passkey is Weak: Phishing the Unphishable
talks.teaser: Demonstrates an effective phishing attack vector against synced passkeys and outlines operational safeguards for enterprise passkey deployments.
talks.summary:
The Promise and Reality of Passkeys

FIDO2 passkeys are widely promoted as the definitive solution to phishing, leveraging public-key cryptography and origin-bound credentials to prevent credential harvesting attacks.

Phishing Vectors Against Synced Passkeys

Chad Spensky demonstrates a practical attack chain targeting consumer-synced passkey ecosystems. By manipulating device enrollment flows and user trust assumptions, attackers can induce users into delegating access or pairing unauthorized synchronization devices.

Social Engineering and Device Pairing Exploits

Attacking the passkey ecosystem shifts the adversary focus from password harvesting to credential syncing mechanisms, QR-code authentication flows, and account recovery handoffs.

Recommendations for Secure Passkey Implementation

Enterprises adopting passkeys must configure strict device attestation policies, mandate hardware security keys for high-privilege roles, and educate users on verifying cross-device pairing prompts.

talks.title: Bare Metal Reverse Engineering
talks.teaser: Presents a structured Ghidra methodology for reverse engineering stripped ARM Cortex bare-metal and FreeRTOS embedded binaries using SVD and BSim plugins.
talks.summary:
Challenges of Bare-Metal Firmware Analysis

Reverse engineering stripped bare-metal firmware and RTOS binaries on ARM Cortex platforms is notoriously difficult due to the absence of symbol tables, dynamic loaders, and standard file formats.

Mapping Board Support Packages via SVD Loader

Using the SVD (System View Description) loader plugin in Ghidra, analysts map memory-mapped hardware peripheral registers directly to MCU hardware specifications, instantly contextualizing hardware control routines.

Deconstructing the Hardware Abstraction Layer

Custom type recovery scripts and function pattern matching allow researchers to identify hardware initialization sequences, peripheral clock gating, and GPIO driver logic without source code.

RTOS Kernel Reconstruction with BSim

Applying Ghidra’s BSim plugin facilitates signature matching against FreeRTOS and other embedded kernels, recovering task creation routines, scheduler priorities, and inter-process communication constructs in complex firmware.

talks.title: Dead Reckoning: Hijacking Marine Autopilots
talks.teaser: Discloses an unauthenticated firmware update vulnerability in marine autopilots, allowing arbitrary CAN injection via NMEA 2000 chart plotters.
talks.summary:
Vulnerabilities in Marine Navigation Computers

Autopilot systems aboard commercial and recreational vessels translate navigation course data into physical rudder actuations over NMEA 2000 CAN networks, operating as critical cyber-physical bridges.

Unauthenticated Firmware Update Flaws

Carson Green and Rik Chatterjee demonstrate how a popular marine autopilot computer accepts unsigned firmware update files (.swup) via SD card slots or networked chart plotters without cryptographic validation or hardware authentication.

Persistent Code Execution and CAN Injection

Crafting a malicious update package allows attackers to gain persistent firmware-level execution on the autopilot hardware, enabling arbitrary CAN packet injection, course spoofing, and remote rudder disruption across the vessel's NMEA 2000 bus.

Remediation for Marine Control Systems

Mitigating marine firmware hijacking requires enforcing cryptographic signature verification in bootloaders, disabling unauthenticated network update mechanisms, and implementing CAN bus intrusion detection.

talks.title: Prompt Scan Exploit AI’s Journey Through 0Days and 1000 Bugs
talks.teaser: Chronicles the deployment of XBOW, an autonomous AI offensive agent that discovered over 200 open-source vulnerabilities and submitted 1,000 bug bounty reports.
talks.summary:
Autonomous AI in Offensive Security

The development of autonomous AI agents capable of end-to-end vulnerability research represents a major milestone in automated security testing.

Architecture of the XBOW Offensive Agent

XBOW integrates large language models with specialized dynamic analysis environments, code scanners, and exploit generators, autonomously exploring web and software attack surfaces without human intervention.

Real-World Vulnerability Discoveries and Impact

Deploying XBOW against real-world targets resulted in the discovery of over 200 security flaws across open-source projects and the submission of more than 1,000 bug bounty reports, earning top rankings on major bounty platforms.

Implications for the Future of Vulnerability Research

The success of autonomous AI agents highlights the accelerating pace of vulnerability discovery, necessitating automated defensive remediation pipelines and AI-driven patch generation.

talks.title: Referral Beware, Your Rewards Are Mine
talks.teaser: Uncovers client-side gadgets, race conditions, and business logic flaws hidden within referral and reward systems across major bug bounty programs.
talks.summary:
The Overlooked Attack Surface of Referral Systems

Referral and reward programs are ubiquitous in consumer web applications but are frequently viewed by bug bounty hunters as routine functionality with minimal security impact.

Business Logic and Race Condition Vulnerabilities

Whit Taylor demonstrates how concurrent API requests and flawed database state transactions allow attackers to exploit race conditions, claiming unlimited referral credits and bypassing payout limits.

Client-Side Gadgets and Exploit Chaining

Improperly sanitized referral parameters introduce client-side path traversal and cookie-injection gadgets that can be chained with other client-side flaws to execute account takeovers.

Securing Reward and Referral Architectures

Defending promotional and referral workflows requires enforcing strict database row locking, validating referral token state idempotently, and sanitizing all client-side redirect parameters.

talks.title: The depths that marketers will plummet to
talks.teaser: Exposes server-side data harvesting techniques developed by digital marketing agencies to track consumers across smart TVs, devices, and ISPs without cookies.
talks.summary:
The Post-Cookie Tracking Landscape

As major web browsers deprecate third-party cookies, the multi-trillion-dollar digital advertising industry has engineered invasive server-side tracking mechanisms to maintain granular consumer surveillance.

Server-Side Data Harvesting Across Device Layers

Drawing from insider experience at a major independent marketing firm, the speaker reveals how agencies correlate user activity across streaming platforms, smart TVs, mobile operating systems, and ISP-level network data.

Evasion of Privacy Controls and Consent Frameworks

Server-side data aggregation bypasses client-side ad blockers and browser privacy protections, packaging invasive identity resolution and cross-device graph matching under the guise of first-party data management.

Technical Countermeasures and Regulatory Oversight

Combating omnipresent behavioral tracking requires consumer network-level filtering, encrypted DNS adoption, and rigorous legal enforcement against deceptive data aggregation practices.

talks.title: Deploying Deception in Depth for ICS
talks.teaser: Presents strategies for designing and deploying cyber deception across industrial control systems using the MITRE Engage framework, focused on APT44 TTPs.
talks.summary:
Cyber Deception in Critical Infrastructure

Deploying defensive deception within Industrial Control Systems (ICS) provides high-fidelity early warning alerts and alters adversary economics by injecting decoys into operational networks.

Operationalizing the MITRE Engage Framework

Brent Muir outlines how industrial defenders can adapt the MITRE Engage framework to map deception activities directly to adversary goals, establishing intentional decoys across OT DMZs and control zones.

Case Study: Defending Against APT44 TTPs

Focusing on threat actor APT44 (Sandworm), the presentation illustrates how emulated programmable logic controllers (PLCs), synthetic industrial protocol responders, and deceptive engineering workstations trap sophisticated attackers.

Engineering Considerations and Safety Guardrails

Designing OT deception requires strict safety controls to prevent honeypot systems from interfering with real-time industrial processes or creating operational hazards.

talks.title: VDP in Aviation: How it Shouldn't be Done!
talks.teaser: Shares firsthand experiences navigating vulnerability disclosure programs in the aviation industry, highlighting common pitfalls and best practices.
talks.summary:
Vulnerability Disclosure Dynamics in Aviation

Vulnerability Disclosure Programs (VDPs) in the aviation sector operate under intense regulatory scrutiny and safety sensitivities, creating friction between independent researchers and aircraft manufacturers.

Firsthand Perspectives from Submissions and Triage

Matt Gaffney shares real-world case studies from both submitting and receiving vulnerability disclosures within the aerospace industry, illustrating how bureaucratic delays and legal threats undermine constructive security research.

Common Institutional Pitfalls

Key shortcomings include ambiguous scope definitions, defensive legal posturing, failure to provide receipt acknowledgments, and lack of safe harbor protections for good-faith researchers.

Frameworks for Constructive Aerospace VDPs

Improving aviation vulnerability handling requires adopting standardized ISO/IEC 29147 disclosure practices, establishing dedicated aerospace CERT channels, and fostering open dialogue with the research community.

talks.title: How API Flaws Led to Admin Access to 1k+ USA Dealers & Control of Yr Car
talks.teaser: Reveals critical API vulnerabilities in a major automotive dealer platform that allowed national admin account creation and remote vehicle command access.
talks.summary:
Centralized Dealer Management Platforms

Automotive dealerships across the United States rely on centralized software platforms to manage inventory, service appointments, customer records, and connected vehicle features.

Discovering Broken Object Level Authorization Flaws

Eaton Zveare identified fundamental access control vulnerabilities in a leading automaker's dealer platform APIs. Unauthenticated parameter tampering allowed researchers to elevate privileges and create national administrative accounts.

Remote Vehicle Telematics Compromise

With national administrator access, researchers could query customer profiles, retrieve vehicle identification numbers (VINs), and transmit remote commands to lock, unlock, start, and track thousands of customer vehicles nationwide.

Lessons for Connected Automotive Ecosystems

Securing automotive dealer management portals demands strict API authentication, multi-factor authorization on administrative endpoints, and rigorous architectural reviews of third-party vendor platforms.

talks.title: Context Aware Anomaly Detection in Automotive CAN Without Decoding
talks.teaser: Introduces a sequence-learning approach that analyzes inter-signal correlations in raw CAN bus payloads to detect stealthy contextual automotive attacks.
talks.summary:
Limitations of Traditional Automotive CAN Anomaly Detectors

Traditional CAN bus intrusion detection systems rely on message frequency tracking or require proprietary DBC decoding files to inspect signal contents. However, sophisticated attackers can inject plausible payloads that blend into expected frequencies.

Context-Aware Sequence Learning on Raw Payloads

Ravi Rajput introduces a deep sequence-learning model that analyzes temporal correlations and contextual relationships across raw CAN payloads without requiring proprietary reverse engineering of message structures.

Detecting Contextual Manipulation Attacks

By learning multi-signal correlations (such as vehicle speed relative to wheel tick sensors and steering angle), the model detects stealthy state manipulation attacks that traditional rule-based detectors miss.

Validation on Automotive Datasets and Testbeds

Evaluating the architecture against real-world vehicular CAN traffic and simulated attack benchmarks demonstrated high detection accuracy and low latency suitable for real-time in-vehicle deployment.

talks.title: Vulns to End Your Space Mission
talks.teaser: Demonstrates proof-of-concept exploits across ground control software and onboard satellite components that grant unauthorized spacecraft control.
talks.summary:
Expanding Attack Surfaces in Space Missions

Modern space missions integrate specialized hardware and software components communicating across custom ground-to-space protocols. Vulnerabilities anywhere in this chain can result in total mission loss.

Vulnerability Analysis of Ground Control Segments

Researchers identified critical flaws across ground station control software, telemetry servers, and antenna controllers, enabling unauthenticated remote command injection into satellite uplinks.

Exploiting Onboard Spacecraft Firmware

Inspecting onboard spacecraft software revealed memory corruption bugs and unauthenticated debugging interfaces in flight computers. Proof-of-concept exploits demonstrated the ability to hijack attitude control and disrupt satellite subsystems.

Hardening Guidelines for Aerospace Missions

Securing space infrastructure requires end-to-end cryptographic command authentication, memory-safe flight software architectures, and rigorous penetration testing before launch.

talks.title: There and Back Again: Detecting OT Devices Across Protocol Gateways
talks.teaser: Details network discovery tradecraft for enumerating OT assets behind protocol translation gateways using CIP message forwarding and DNP3 discovery.
talks.summary:
The Reality of OT/IT Network Convergence

Industrial Control Systems (ICS) increasingly adopt commodity TCP/IP networking, connecting proprietary field devices to enterprise networks through protocol translation gateways.

Visibility Challenges Behind Protocol Gateways

Protocol gateways translate standard TCP/IP traffic into proprietary serial or fieldbus communications. Standard IT network scanners cannot enumerate devices residing behind these gateway boundaries, creating major asset visibility blind spots.

CIP Message Forwarding and DNP3 Discovery

Rob King details practical techniques for querying devices through gateways, demonstrating how Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) routing and DNP3 address discovery mechanisms can be leveraged to enumerate hidden field assets.

Actionable Reconnaissance for Industrial Defenders

Implementing protocol-aware discovery techniques enables defenders to build accurate asset inventories, identify legacy endpoints, and enforce proper network segmentation across industrial facilities.

talks.title: Hacking Space to Defend It: Generating IoBs with SPARTA
talks.teaser: Applies offensive techniques from the SPARTA framework to generate behavioral indicators (IoBs) and design realistic intrusion detection systems for spacecraft.
talks.summary:
The Need for Threat-Informed Space Defense

While the SPARTA (Space Attack Research and Tactic Analysis) framework cataloged spaceborne cyber threats, mission operators needed empirical methods to detect these attacks in operational environments.

Simulating Space Attacks and TTP Replay

Brandon Bailey details hands-on offensive testing against simulated spacecraft flight software and telemetry buses to observe behavioral anomalies and telemetry patterns generated during active attacks.

Generating Indicators of Behavior (IoBs)

From these simulations, researchers developed concrete Indicators of Behavior (IoBs)—such as unexpected CPU scheduling spikes, anomalous telemetry packet rates, and out-of-sequence command verifications—tailored to resource-constrained flight computers.

Designing Spaceborne Intrusion Detection Systems

Integrating data-driven IoBs into spacecraft IDS architectures enables real-time threat detection aboard satellites without overloading onboard computing resources.

talks.title: Back to Basics: Building Resilient Cyber Defenses
talks.teaser: Critiques viral but ineffective cybersecurity advice, highlighting practical, foundational defensive measures to mitigate high-likelihood digital threats.
talks.summary:
Evaluating Viral Cybersecurity Advice

In the wake of high-profile cyberattacks and data breaches, viral security advice often spreads across social media. However, much of this advice focuses on obscure edge cases while ignoring foundational security hygiene.

Analyzing High-Profile Threats vs. Everyday Risks

Yael Grauer compares sensationalized threat scenarios with the everyday risks individuals and organizations actually face, such as credential stuffing, SIM swapping, and basic phishing.

Practical and Actionable Defensive Steps

Effective defense centers on proven core controls: adopting password managers, enabling hardware-backed multi-factor authentication, keeping software updated, and auditing account recovery workflows.

Building Proactive and Reactive Resilience

Establishing practical response plans and cultivating security habits before incidents occur ensures long-term digital privacy and resilience against persistent threat actors.

talks.title: Creating a Virtual Ship Environment Optimized for Cybersecurity Use
talks.teaser: Explores the architecture of a hybrid virtual ship simulator augmented with marine engine and instrument emulators for maritime security research.
talks.summary:
Limitations of Standard Maritime Simulators

Commercial maritime simulators are designed to train deck officers for navigational certifications (STCW) and lack the underlying network architectures necessary for cybersecurity assessments and research.

Hybrid Virtual Ship Architecture

Jeff Greer presents research from UNCW establishing a hybrid virtual ship environment that integrates full-mission bridge simulations with specialized hardware emulators and virtualized industrial controllers.

Simulating Engine Controls and Bridge Instruments

By augmenting commercial simulators (such as the Unitest Winterthur X92 marine engine simulator) with virtualized CAN and NMEA interfaces, researchers can inject cyberattacks and observe realistic physical vessel responses.

Applications in Education and Security Research

The hybrid testbed provides a safe, reproducible environment for training maritime defenders, testing intrusion detection algorithms, and evaluating shipboard cyber resilience.

talks.title: Bio Cryptography is the Game Genie in a post quantum dystopia
talks.teaser: Explores bio-cryptography and biological key generation as decentralized cryptographic primitives resilient against post-quantum computational attacks.
talks.summary:
Post-Quantum Cryptographic Vulnerabilities

As quantum computing advances threaten standard asymmetric encryption algorithms, researchers are exploring biological and physiological data sources to generate dynamic, decentralized cryptographic keys.

Principles of Bio-Cryptography

Bio-cryptography combines unique, high-entropy biological signals (such as genomic sequences or dynamic physiological metrics) with error-correcting codes to derive reproducible cryptographic keying material.

Decentralized Key Derivation and Verification

By grounding key generation in biological processes, systems eliminate centralized key escrow and static credential storage, creating self-sovereign authentication mechanisms resistant to quantum cryptanalysis.

Ethical Considerations and Future Applications

Deploying bio-cryptographic primitives requires addressing biological data privacy, template protection, and ensuring ethical boundaries in biometric security deployments.

talks.title: Evolution of Drain Attacks
talks.teaser: Traces the evolution of wallet draining attacks across Ethereum, Solana, and TON, demonstrating token spoofing exploits and transaction tracking methods.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of Cryptocurrency Wallet Drainers

Wallet draining attacks represent one of the most widespread financial fraud vectors in the Web3 ecosystem, targeting cryptocurrency holders across Ethereum, Solana, and TON blockchains.

Evolution from Approval Abuse to Token Spoofing

Early drainers relied on deceptive ERC-20 'setApprovalForAll' contract calls. Modern drainer kits employ sophisticated token spoofing, off-chain signature manipulation (such as Permit and Permit2 abuse), and multi-chain transaction batching.

Laundering Networks and Illicit Flow Tracking

Analyzing blockchain transaction graphs reveals how drainer operators move stolen assets through cross-chain bridges, decentralized mixers, and money laundering funnels to cash out proceeds.

Wallet Security and Defensive Monitoring

Mitigating drainer attacks requires wallet interfaces to provide human-readable transaction simulation, revoke dormant contract allowances, and flag known phishing domains.

talks.title: Unveiling IoT Vulns: From Backdoors to Bureaucracy
talks.teaser: Examines over 50 real-world IoT vulnerability cases featuring hardcoded backdoors and discusses systemic barriers in reporting flaws to vendors and CERTs.
talks.summary:
Widespread Vulnerabilities in the IoT Ecosystem

Analyzing over 50 real-world IoT vulnerability disclosures reveals persistent systemic security flaws across commercial routers, industrial cameras, and environmental monitoring devices.

Hardcoded Backdoors and Predictable Credentials

Critical vulnerabilities, including CVE-2024-48271 (CVSS 9.8) and CVE-2025-1143, demonstrate vendor-embedded backdoors, hardcoded root credentials, and unauthenticated management consoles that grant remote attackers global device control.

Risks to Critical Infrastructure

Poorly secured commercial IoT devices deployed in municipal water plants, ATM networks, and transportation systems provide direct pivot points for criminal scammers and nation-state threat actors.

Bureaucratic Barriers in Responsible Disclosure

Kai-Ching Wang and Chiao-Lin Yu share the challenges of navigating vendor denials, unresponsive CNAs, and multi-year reporting delays, advocating for reforms in international vulnerability coordination.

talks.title: Crossing the Line: Advanced Techniques to Breach the OT DMZ
talks.teaser: Explores offensive tradecraft for bypassing DMZ segmentation and pivoting from enterprise footholds into industrial control networks.
talks.summary:
The OT DMZ as a Critical Security Boundary

The demilitarized zone (DMZ) separating enterprise IT networks from operational technology (OT) control zones is designed to enforce strict isolation. However, operational conveniences often introduce severe segmentation weaknesses.

Pivoting from Enterprise Footholds

Christopher Nourrie demonstrates how red team operators leverage initial IT access to identify and abuse misconfigured remote access solutions, jump hosts, Citrix gateways, and RDP relays spanning the IT/OT boundary.

Lateral Movement and Credential Abuse in the DMZ

Techniques for proxying traffic, abusing dual-homed systems, and extracting cached administrative credentials within the DMZ allow attackers to bypass intended Purdue Model network boundaries.

Hardening Industrial Perimeter Defenses

Defending the OT perimeter requires eliminating dual-homed jump hosts, enforcing dedicated multi-factor authentication on industrial access portals, and monitoring east-west network traffic across the DMZ.

talks.title: Let AI Autogenerate Neural ASR Rules for OT Attacks via NLP
talks.teaser: Introduces Suspicious2Vec, an NLP-based multimodal AI model that establishes baseline industrial operations to generate neural attack surface reduction rules.
talks.summary:
Living-Off-the-Land Attacks in Industrial Networks

Sophisticated threat actors targeting industrial control systems (such as Sandworm in Ukraine) routinely abuse benign OT-specific protocols, LOLBins, and native engineering utilities to evade conventional EDR detection.

Suspicious2Vec: Multimodal AI for Industrial Baselines

Mars Cheng and Jr Wei-Huang present Suspicious2Vec, an NLP-inspired multimodal AI framework that learns contextual baselines of normal factory operations by converting industrial system behaviors into numerical vector embeddings.

Autogenerating Neural Attack Surface Reduction Rules

Trained on a massive dataset of 2,000,000 operational events and malware profiles from VirusTotal, the model autogenerates neural Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules that accurately differentiate benign operational anomalies from malicious Living-Off-the-Land techniques.

Validation on Factory Environments

Deploying Suspicious2Vec across operational manufacturing plants successfully detected 12 novel variant OT malware strains across more than 52,000 program files with minimal false positives.

talks.title: The PowerPoint Glove
talks.teaser: Walks through hacking the retro NES Power Glove with an ESP32 microcontroller to build a custom Bluetooth presentation controller.
talks.summary:
Hacking Retro Gaming Accessories

The iconic Nintendo Power Glove, released for the NES in 1989, remains a beloved cult accessory. Modern microcontrollers allow enthusiasts to repurpose its sensors for practical computing tasks.

Reverse Engineering the NES Controller Protocol

Parsia Hakimian breaks down the proprietary shift register communication protocol used by the original NES controller port, explaining how flex sensors and keypad buttons report physical state.

Interfacing with the ESP32 Microcontroller

Wiring the Power Glove to an ESP32 development board enables reading button scancodes and flex sensor resistance in real time, translating gestures and button presses into standard HID keyboard commands.

Building a Wireless Bluetooth Presentation Tool

Configuring the ESP32 as a Bluetooth HID device turns the Power Glove into an interactive PowerPoint remote controller, demonstrating accessible microcontroller hacking for conference presentations.

talks.title: QRAMM: The Cryptographic Migration to a Post Quantum World
talks.teaser: Introduces the Quantum Readiness Assurance Maturity Model (QRAMM), an open-source framework assessing organizational agility for post-quantum migrations.
talks.summary:
Navigating Post-Quantum Cryptographic Migration

With NIST finalizing post-quantum cryptography standards, enterprises face a massive operational challenge in transitioning legacy encryption, digital signatures, and key exchange protocols to quantum-resistant alternatives.

The Quantum Readiness Assurance Maturity Model (QRAMM)

Emily Fane and Abdel Sy Fane introduce QRAMM, an open-source framework designed to help organizations assess their post-quantum readiness across four core dimensions: cryptographic visibility, data protection, technical implementation, and governance.

Achieving Cryptographic Agility

QRAMM emphasizes cryptographic agility—the architectural ability to swap cryptographic algorithms and certificate structures seamlessly without re-engineering underlying software applications.

Practical Roadmap for Enterprise Adoption

Implementing QRAMM provides structured maturity roadmaps, risk assessment metrics, and compliance guidelines to help security leaders navigate post-quantum migration deadlines.

talks.title: Intro to Common Industrial Protocol Exploitation
talks.teaser: Introduces the fundamentals of the Common Industrial Protocol (CIP) used in factory automation and demonstrates techniques for industrial protocol testing.

talks.title: Cloned Vishing : A case study
talks.teaser: Presents empirical results from a university research study evaluating user vulnerability and defensive safeguards against AI voice-cloned vishing attacks.

talks.title: The Missing Link: Draytek’s New RCEs Complete the Chain
talks.teaser: Discloses two unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities in Draytek routers (CVE-2024-51138 and CVE-2024-51139) that enable full edge device takeovers.
talks.summary:
Edge Router Vulnerabilities in Corporate Networks

Draytek routers are widely deployed as edge gateways across enterprise and small business networks. Their internet-exposed management interfaces make them prime targets for botnets and state-sponsored threat actors.

Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution Flaws

Researchers disclose two critical zero-day vulnerabilities in Draytek firmware: CVE-2024-51138 (a buffer overflow in STUN CGI handling) and CVE-2024-51139 (an integer overflow in CGI query parsing).

End-to-End Exploitation and Persistence Chain

Chaining these RCE vulnerabilities with previously documented firmware persistence techniques allows unauthenticated attackers to achieve root access from the WAN interface and install persistent backdoors.

Tooling and Edge Device Defense

The researchers release Draytek Arsenal, an open-source firmware analysis toolkit, emphasizing the necessity of rapid edge device patching and disabling external management interfaces.

talks.title: Smart Bus Smart Hacking: Free WiFi to Total Control
talks.teaser: Demonstrates an attack chain starting from passenger public Wi-Fi to breach vehicular routers, hijack on-board units, and manipulate smart bus displays.
talks.summary:
Connected Public Transit Architecture

Modern smart buses integrate On-Board Units (OBUs), passenger Wi-Fi routers, automated fare collection, and Advanced Public Transportation Services (APTS) communicating over internal vehicle networks.

From Passenger Wi-Fi to Vehicular Router Compromise

Kai Ching Wang and Chiao-Lin Yu demonstrate over ten vulnerabilities discovered across connected transit systems, showing how connecting to unsegmented passenger Wi-Fi allows attackers to exploit vehicular routers and access private internal subnets.

Hijacking ADAS, APTS, and Onboard Displays

Once inside the vehicular network, attackers can manipulate LED route displays, intercept passenger and driver telemetry, spoof GPS coordinates, and pivot to transport company backend API servers.

Policy and Supply Chain Recommendations

Addressing smart transit vulnerabilities requires enforcing strict network isolation between public Wi-Fi and vehicle telemetry, removing vendor backdoors, and updating public transit cybersecurity specifications.

talks.title: Vibe School: Making dumb devices smart with AI
talks.teaser: Demonstrates using AI-assisted coding to reverse engineer conventional hardware and integrate legacy sensors into Home Assistant.
talks.summary:
Democratizing Smart Home Integration with AI

Commercial smart home sensors and specialized environmental monitors often carry high prices, while inexpensive conventional hardware lacks network connectivity. AI-assisted programming lowers the barrier to bridging legacy hardware into modern smart home platforms.

Sniffing Sensor Signals and Protocol Analysis

Katie Paxton Fear demonstrates how to intercept and decode communication signals from an inexpensive conventional weather station using basic hardware sniffers and radio receivers.

AI-Assisted Microcontroller Firmware Development

Using generative AI models (such as Gemini) to write C++ firmware for microcontrollers (ESP32 / Arduino), researchers rapidly translate raw sensor telemetry into structured MQTT payloads.

Integrating Legacy Hardware into Home Assistant

Connecting the custom firmware to Home Assistant creates an automated, low-cost smart weather station, illustrating how 'vibe coding' empowers makers to customize connected devices.

talks.title: The Things know What You Did Last Session
talks.teaser: Examines corporate threat investigations, from detecting robotic fingerprint timecard fraud to uncovering remote North Korean IT contractor networks.
talks.summary:
Investigating Physical and Digital Enterprise Threats

Corporate threat investigations routinely span physical hardware manipulation, digital forensics, and international cybercrime schemes. Investigator Will Baggett shares real-world case studies from complex internal inquiries.

Automated Hardware Timecard Fraud

In a bizarre fraud scheme, an on-site contractor engineered a robotic device with synthetic flesh to automatically press a biometric fingerprint reader daily on a hidden iPhone, faking physical attendance on corporate visitor networks.

Chip-Off Extraction of Voting Machine Hardware

Baggett details IoT forensic investigations involving chip-off flash memory extraction from prototype voting machines, demonstrating hardware extraction techniques used for national security assessments.

Hunting North Korean IT Worker Fraud Networks

Investigating remote IT contractor networks revealed North Korean operatives utilizing piKVM switches, VPN routers, and virtual machine tunneling to bypass enterprise identity verification and funnel earnings back to DPRK state operations.

Forensic Indicators and Mitigation Strategies

Detecting contractor fraud requires correlating network telemetry, analyzing device fingerprints, monitoring anomalous VPN connections, and conducting rigorous identity verification interviews.

talks.title: Access Control Done Right the First Time
talks.teaser: Provides practical engineering best practices for deploying physical access control systems, covering supervised wiring, tamper resistance, and badge encryption.
talks.summary:
Pitfalls of Minimum Viable Access Control

Physical Access Control Systems (PACS) are frequently installed using minimum viable product configurations that leave doors vulnerable to simple physical bypasses and electronic credential cloning.

Supervised Wiring and Tamper Resistance

Tim Clevenger explains the critical importance of supervised reader wiring and end-of-line resistors, which detect when cables are cut or spliced by physical red teamers attempting inline badge cloning.

Selecting Clone-Resistant Credentials

Replacing vulnerable legacy 125 kHz proximity cards (such as standard HID Prox) with modern encrypted smartcards (like MIFARE DESFire EV3 or HID Seos) prevents unauthorized badge duplication.

Hardening Controllers and Operational Maintenance

Securing access control infrastructure requires locking controller enclosures, isolating management networks, maintaining accurate badge revocation records, and routinely testing door position switches.

talks.title: Smart Devices, Dumb Resets:Testing Firmware Persistence in Commercial IoT
talks.teaser: Investigates retail returns sanitization, proving that modified IoT firmware persists across store resales and creates supply chain backdoor vectors.
talks.summary:
Supply Chain Vulnerabilities in Returned Retail Electronics

Consumer electronics retailers routinely process returned smart home devices and resell them as open-box or refurbished goods. However, retailer sanitization and reset procedures are rarely audited for cybersecurity risks.

Experimental Methodology: Planting Custom Firmware

Matei Jose purchased commercial IoT devices from major retail stores, flashed custom firmware embedding a persistent callback beacon, and returned the products following standard return procedures.

Persistence Across Retail Restocking Pipelines

Repurchasing the returned items revealed that major retailers failed to properly wipe or reflash device firmware, allowing custom backdoor firmware to remain fully intact and operational.

Risks of Retail Supply Chain Implants

This sanitization failure creates a viable attack vector for adversaries to deploy persistent IoT botnet implants, exfiltration tools, or surveillance backdoors directly into consumer supply chains.

Mitigation Strategies for Manufacturers and Retailers

Addressing retail supply chain persistence requires manufacturers to implement cryptographic firmware attestation, enforce hardware-level factory reset fuses, and mandate automated retailer device sanitization.

talks.title: Critically Neglected: Cybersecurity for buildings
talks.teaser: Explores systemic cybersecurity vulnerabilities in building management systems, HVAC controls, and physical facility automation networks.
talks.summary:
The Overlooked Landscape of Building Automation

Modern commercial facilities rely on Building Management Systems (BMS) to control HVAC systems, power distribution, fire suppression, and physical access. These automation systems are frequently deployed with minimal cybersecurity oversight.

Insecure Protocols in Facility Automation

Protocols like BACnet, Modbus, and LonWorks were designed decades ago without authentication or encryption. When building automation networks are connected to corporate IT or exposed to the internet, attackers can manipulate physical environmental controls.

Case Studies of Building Compromises

Thomas Pope reviews real-world security assessments where compromised HVAC controllers allowed attackers to pivot into corporate subnets, manipulate datacenter cooling, or trigger physical facility lockouts.

Hardening Facility Control Systems

Securing building automation requires isolating BMS networks from corporate IT, deploying protocol-aware firewalls, disabling unneeded remote management portals, and establishing strict vendor maintenance access controls.

talks.title: Incident Response from a Maritime Sysadmin’s War Room
talks.teaser: Breaks down executive and technical incident response perspectives following real-world cyber incidents at the Marine Exchange of Southern California.
talks.summary:
The Crucial Role of Maritime Exchanges

The Marine Exchange of Southern California manages vessel traffic service and harbor safety across major seaport complexes, serving as an indispensable operational hub for maritime logistics.

Executive and Leadership Perspectives on Cyber Incidents

Executive Director Kit Louttit shares the strategic and operational considerations that arise during active cyber threats, focusing on stakeholder communication, business continuity, and maritime safety.

Firsthand Technical Incident Response in the War Room

Senior Systems Administrator Steve Winston breaks down the technical triage, log analysis, and rapid containment actions executed during incident response in the Marine Exchange's war room.

Building Resilient Maritime IT/OT Infrastructure

Lessons learned emphasize the necessity of cross-functional disaster recovery drills, robust network segmentation, and continuous monitoring to maintain harbor traffic services during critical outages.

talks.title: Hard Hat Brigade Creations Q&A
talks.teaser: Hard Hat Brigade creators discuss custom electronic construction hat builds, wearable modifications, and community maker projects.

talks.title: One Modem to Brick Them All -Vulns in EV Charging Comms
talks.teaser: Discloses vulnerabilities in QCA 7000 HomePlug modems used across CCS and NACS EV charging systems that enable communication hijacking and denial of service.
talks.summary:
Power-Line Communication in EV Charging Systems

Electric Vehicle (EV) charging systems rely on Combined Charging System (CCS) and North American Charging Standard (NACS) protocols, which utilize HomePlug Green PHY power-line communication (PLC) for vehicle-to-grid data exchange.

Vulnerabilities in the QCA 7000 Modem Series

Jan Berens and Marcell Szakaly analyze the widely used Qualcomm QCA 7000 modem series, uncovering multiple critical vulnerabilities in PLC message processing and firmware execution.

Remote Communication Hijacking and Denial of Service

Exploiting flaws in HomePlug link negotiation allows attackers to intercept charging session telemetry at a distance, inject spoofed control commands, or trigger persistent denial-of-service conditions that prevent vehicle charging.

Firmware Reverse Engineering and Code Execution

Reverse engineering the QCA 7000 firmware revealed memory corruption vulnerabilities enabling arbitrary code execution on the modem hardware, highlighting urgent security needs across global EV charging infrastructure.
